items.title: Jimmy Heath interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, September 8, 2014
items.q: I remember Theodore “Fats” Navarro. Great trumpeter.

ctx.x: Well said. I’ve had a debate sometimes with musicians about, are there wrong notes when you improvise?

Well the way I look at improvisation, you know you can step out of the basic chord pattern if you make the connections. In other words, life is about connections. Everything musically is about connections. Socially it’s about connections. Connections is one of the biggest words in the English language. You’ve got to make a connection. And that’s what I’m talking about. If you see, like I remember Theodore “Fats” Navarro. Great trumpeter. And Fats used to play — if a woman walked in with a red dress on [scats]…

Oh, that’s terrific. Sometimes when I think about the history of jazz it has moved so fast it seems like. And I was remembering some of the things that Coltrane and Ornette Coleman did in the 60s. And now that seems like, wow, what is that, 50 years ago. I wonder what your reaction was to records like “Ascension” and free jazz.
